# ali-nuxt-toolkit — full reference

> Five independently-installable, type-driven packages for Vue 3 and Nuxt 3+. A typed `fetch` client, Web-Crypto encryption, layout-based route middleware, a headless international tel input, and measured skeleton loaders. Each package ships a framework-agnostic `./core` entry alongside its Nuxt module or Vue component.

This file is a single-file reference designed for LLM consumption. It inlines install + minimal usage for every package so a model can get productive without follow-up fetches. For richer prose, props/events/slots tables, theming tokens, and accessibility notes, follow the per-package links listed in `llms.txt`.

Supported runtimes: Node ≥ 20.19, Nuxt ≥ 3.12, Vue ≥ 3.4. The `@alikhalilll/a-*` UI packages are plain Vue 3 components — they work outside Nuxt too, via `unplugin-vue-components` resolvers.

---

## Design contract (repo-wide)

Every package in this repo adheres to the same rules. When writing code that uses or extends the toolkit, follow these too — reviewers enforce them:

- **Types first.** Public API is defined by exported types, implementations second. Discriminated unions over boolean flags.
- **Pure-function first.** Side effects (DOM reads, `localStorage`, network) are confined to the smallest possible boundary. Walkers, transformers, formatters stay pure and testable.
- **Strategy pattern over `if` chains.** Runtime variants (reveal modes, cache strategies, auth presets) are entries in a dispatch table.
- **Composition over inheritance.** Render-function composition, composables, slot trees — no mixins.
- **SSR-safe.** No `window` / `document` at module scope. Browser-only effects behind `onMounted`. Hydration-stable DOM output.
- **Boundary purity.** Each package's `./core` must not import from its Nuxt module surface and vice versa.
- **Honest `sideEffects`.** Subpath exports (`/core`, `/types`, `/zod`, `/vee-validate`) so unused code doesn't ship.

---

## Install

```bash
# UI components (Vue 3 — work outside Nuxt)
pnpm add @alikhalilll/a-tel-input @alikhalilll/a-ghost-skeleton

# Nuxt modules
pnpm add @alikhalilll/nuxt-api-provider \
         @alikhalilll/nuxt-crypto \
         @alikhalilll/nuxt-auto-middleware
```

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts — add only what you use
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: [
    '@alikhalilll/a-tel-input/nuxt',
    '@alikhalilll/a-ghost-skeleton/nuxt',
    '@alikhalilll/nuxt-api-provider',
    '@alikhalilll/nuxt-crypto',
    '@alikhalilll/nuxt-auto-middleware',
  ],
  css: ['@alikhalilll/a-tel-input/styles.css'],
});
```

For non-Nuxt Vue + Vite consumers, each component package ships a resolver:

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import Components from 'unplugin-vue-components/vite';
import ATelInputResolver from '@alikhalilll/a-tel-input/resolver';
import AGhostSkeletonResolver from '@alikhalilll/a-ghost-skeleton/resolver';

export default {
  plugins: [Components({ resolvers: [ATelInputResolver(), AGhostSkeletonResolver()] })],
};
```

---

## `@alikhalilll/nuxt-api-provider`

Strongly-typed `fetch` client. TanStack-Query-style caching enabled by default (SWR, in-flight deduplication, GC), interceptor chain, retry with exponential backoff, request timeouts, upload + download progress via transparent `XMLHttpRequest` fallback, structured `ApiError` with a cross-realm `isApiError()` guard (uses `Symbol.for(...)` so bundle duplication doesn't break the check).

### Config

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['@alikhalilll/nuxt-api-provider'],
  apiProvider: {
    baseURL: 'https://api.example.com',
    provideName: '$apiProvider',
    defaultTimeoutMs: 20_000,
    retry: { attempts: 2, delayMs: 500, backoff: 2 },
    cache: { staleTime: 60_000, hydrate: true },
    onRequestPath: '~/api/on-request',
    onErrorPath: '~/api/on-error',
  },
});
```

### Usage

```ts
import type { ApiProviderClient } from '@alikhalilll/nuxt-api-provider/types';
export const useApi = (): ApiProviderClient => useNuxtApp().$apiProvider;

// 3rd arg is the query object; null/undefined/'' are skipped, arrays repeat.
const posts = await useApi()<Post[]>('/posts', null, { userId: 1, tag: ['news', 'featured'] });
await useApi()<Post>('/posts', { method: 'POST', body: { userId: 42, title: 'Hello' } });

// Per-call cache control
await useApi()<Stock>('/stocks/AAPL', { cache: false });                 // bypass
await useApi()<User>('/me', { cache: { refetch: true } });               // force refetch
useApi().cache.invalidate((key) => key.includes('/posts'));              // manual invalidate
```

### Behaviour

- Repeated GETs return cached data within `staleTime` (default 30s) without hitting the network.
- After `staleTime`, cached data is returned **and** a background refresh is kicked off (stale-while-revalidate).
- Concurrent identical calls share one in-flight promise (deduplication).
- Mutations are never cached.
- Pass `onRequestProgress` and the client transparently swaps to `XMLHttpRequest` for upload progress — retry, timeout, `AbortSignal`, `ApiError`, and caching keep working identically; the fast path stays on native `fetch`.

### Errors

```ts
import { isApiError } from '@alikhalilll/nuxt-api-provider/types';

try {
  await useApi()<User>('/me');
} catch (e) {
  if (isApiError(e)) {
    // e.status === 0 → network / aborted (no response)
    // e.status >= 400 → HTTP error
    console.error(e.status, e.statusText, e.data);
  }
}
```

### Framework-agnostic core

```ts
import { createApiClient } from '@alikhalilll/nuxt-api-provider/core';

const api = createApiClient({ baseURL: 'https://api.github.com', retry: { attempts: 2 } });
const repo = await api<{ stargazers_count: number }>('/repos/nuxt/nuxt');
```

---

## `@alikhalilll/nuxt-crypto`

Symmetric encryption on the native Web Crypto API. AES-256-GCM + PBKDF2-SHA256 by default, with derived-key caching, pluggable algorithms, and a server-only mode that keeps the passphrase off the browser bundle. PBKDF2 is deliberately slow; cached per-salt derived keys make the second decrypt essentially free.

### Config

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['@alikhalilll/nuxt-crypto'],
  crypto: {
    passphrase: process.env.NUXT_ENCRYPTION_PASSPHRASE ?? '',
    iterations: 100_000,
    keyCacheSize: 64,
    serverOnly: false,       // true → skip client plugin
  },
});
```

### Usage

```ts
const { $crypto } = useNuxtApp();

const payload = await $crypto.encrypt('super-secret');
// → "v1.<saltB64>.<ivB64>.<cipherB64>"

const plain = await $crypto.decrypt(payload);
```

### Device-fingerprint binding

Ties a payload to the browser that created it — a copy of the token in another browser refuses to decrypt. The fingerprint is built from an HttpOnly device-ID cookie, so it survives Wi-Fi ↔ 4G switches, VPN rotations, and IP changes.

### Framework-agnostic core

```ts
import { createCryptoService } from '@alikhalilll/nuxt-crypto/core';

const crypto = await createCryptoService({ passphrase: process.env.ENC_PASS! });
const token = await crypto.encrypt('hi');
const plain = await crypto.decrypt(token);
```

---

## `@alikhalilll/nuxt-auto-middleware`

Declarative, layout-based route middleware. Map layouts → middlewares once in `nuxt.config.ts` and the module generates a single global route middleware that dispatches the right chain on each navigation. Glob (`*`, `**`, `?`) and `RegExp` patterns are both supported.

### Config

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['@alikhalilll/nuxt-auto-middleware'],
  autoMiddleware: {
    groups: {
      auth: ['auth', 'verify-role'],
      adminOnly: ['auth', 'verify-role', 'require-admin'],
    },
    rules: [
      { layouts: ['default'], middlewares: ['log-activity'] },
      { layouts: ['dashboard', 'dashboard/*'], middlewares: ['@auth'] },
      { layouts: ['admin', 'admin/**'], middlewares: ['@adminOnly'] },
    ],
  },
});
```

### Per-page overrides

```ts
definePageMeta({ middlewares: ['custom'] }); // replaces the layout chain for this page
```

The module emits a **typed registry** so middleware typos are compile errors, not silent routing bugs.

---

## `@alikhalilll/a-tel-input`

Headless international telephone input. Starts as a single clean input — the country picker stays hidden until a number is recognised. Numbers validate against `libphonenumber-js` in real time; the picker is a popover on desktop and a bottom-sheet drawer on mobile (both with a sticky-safe scroll lock). Plugs straight into VeeValidate + Zod with first-class support for async server-side checks.

### Two binding contracts (stay in sync)

```vue
<!-- Single E.164 string — works with VeeValidate and native forms -->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { ATelInput } from '@alikhalilll/a-tel-input';
const phone = ref(''); // → '+201066105963'
</script>
<template>
  <ATelInput v-model="phone" default-country="SA" show-validation />
</template>
```

```vue
<!-- Or split into two v-models: digits-only national + dial code -->
<ATelInput v-model:phone="phone" v-model:country="country" default-country="SA" show-validation />
```

### VeeValidate + Zod

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useForm, Field as VeeField } from 'vee-validate';
import { toTypedSchema } from '@vee-validate/zod';
import { z } from 'zod';
import { ATelInput } from '@alikhalilll/a-tel-input';
import { zPhone } from '@alikhalilll/a-tel-input/zod';

const { handleSubmit } = useForm({
  validationSchema: toTypedSchema(z.object({ phone: zPhone() })),
});
</script>

<template>
  <form @submit="handleSubmit(onSubmit)">
    <VeeField v-slot="{ field, errors }" name="phone">
      <ATelInput
        v-bind="field"
        :error="errors[0]"
        :aria-invalid="!!errors.length"
        default-country="SA"
        show-validation
      />
    </VeeField>
  </form>
</template>
```

### Server-side async validation ("is this phone already registered?")

```ts
import { useForm } from 'vee-validate';
import { toTypedSchema } from '@vee-validate/zod';
import { z } from 'zod';
import { useTelField } from '@alikhalilll/a-tel-input/vee-validate';
import { zPhone } from '@alikhalilll/a-tel-input/zod';

const phoneSchema = zPhone().refine(
  async (value) => {
    if (!value) return true;
    const { exists } = await $fetch('/api/phone/exists', { query: { phone: value } });
    return !exists;
  },
  { message: 'This phone number is already registered.' }
);

const { handleSubmit } = useForm({
  validationSchema: toTypedSchema(z.object({ phone: phoneSchema })),
});

const { phone, country, error, handleBlur, fieldProps, validating } = useTelField('phone', {
  validateOn: 'blur',
});
```

```vue
<ATelInput
  v-model:phone="phone"
  v-model:country="country"
  v-bind="fieldProps"
  :error="error"
  :validating="validating"
  show-validation
  @blur="handleBlur"
/>
```

`:validating` shows a spinner in the field while the server check is in flight; the input stays focusable and `aria-busy="true"` is set for assistive tech.

### Capabilities summary

- Smart country detection: debounced typing + IP / timezone / locale chain on mount.
- Seven libphonenumber failure reasons; per-country format hint.
- Headless slots for every visual region (trigger, chevron, flag, item, search, hint, error).
- i18n + RTL — Arabic-Indic / Persian / Devanagari / Bengali numerals folded to ASCII; country names via `Intl.DisplayNames`.
- SSR-safe, TypeScript-first, web-types for JetBrains IDEs.

---

## `@alikhalilll/a-ghost-skeleton`

Measured skeleton loaders. Hand-authored skeletons drift from the real template as padding changes, font sizes bump, and images load later — the reveal jumps. `AGhostSkeleton` lays your real content out invisibly, measures the live geometry (background, border, radius, box-shadow, text lines, media boxes), and reconstructs a pixel-faithful placeholder from what it saw. One template — the real one — stays the source of truth. Zero cumulative layout shift.

### Minimal example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref, onMounted } from 'vue';

const user = ref<User | null>(null);
const SAMPLE_USER = {
  name: 'Sarah Connor',
  role: 'Chief Mitigation Officer',
  avatar: 'https://example.com/avatar.jpg',
};

onMounted(async () => (user.value = await $fetch('/api/me')));
</script>

<template>
  <AGhostSkeleton :data="user" :sample="SAMPLE_USER" id="user-card">
    <template #default="{ data }">
      <!-- your real template — this is also what the skeleton measures -->
      <div class="card">
        <img :src="data.avatar" />
        <h3>{{ data.name }}</h3>
        <p>{{ data.role }}</p>
      </div>
    </template>
  </AGhostSkeleton>
</template>
```

### States

Four built-in states resolved automatically from the `data` prop (plus a configurable `empty` predicate):

- `loading` — data is null / fetching
- `content` — data resolved and non-empty
- `empty` — resolved but empty (array `[]`, empty string, custom predicate)
- `error` — bound explicitly via the `:error` prop

### Hints (steer the capture)

HTML attributes on elements inside the slot:

- `ask-block` — treat this element as an atomic shape (don't recurse into its children)
- `ask-ignore` — skip this element entirely in the skeleton
- `ask-own` — render this element's own tree verbatim (escape hatch for icons / interactive bits)

### Reveal strategies

Entries in a dispatch table (strategy pattern), selected via `reveal` prop:

- `smart` (default) — reveals by content type: text lines cross-fade, images pop, blocks slide
- `sequence` — top-to-bottom cascade
- `sweep` — diagonal gradient sweep
- `together` — single global crossfade

### Theming

CSS custom properties — override `--ass-base`, `--ass-shimmer`, `--ass-duration`, etc. at any ancestor.

---

## Framework-agnostic cores (recap)

Every Nuxt-module package exposes the same functionality without Nuxt, via `./core` — usable in Node, Bun, Deno, CLIs, and tests. The UI packages (`a-tel-input`, `a-ghost-skeleton`) are plain Vue 3 components and work in any Vue app.

| Package                            | Framework-agnostic entry                    | Shape                                |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `@alikhalilll/nuxt-api-provider`   | `@alikhalilll/nuxt-api-provider/core`       | `createApiClient(options)` function  |
| `@alikhalilll/nuxt-crypto`         | `@alikhalilll/nuxt-crypto/core`             | `createCryptoService(options)` async |
| `@alikhalilll/nuxt-auto-middleware`| (Nuxt-only — routing is Nuxt's concern)     | n/a                                  |
| `@alikhalilll/a-tel-input`         | Vue component — import from the root        | `<ATelInput />`                      |
| `@alikhalilll/a-ghost-skeleton`    | Vue component — import from the root        | `<AGhostSkeleton />`                 |

---

## Repository layout

```
packages/
  api-provider/                     # @alikhalilll/nuxt-api-provider
  crypto/                           # @alikhalilll/nuxt-crypto
  auto-middleware/                  # @alikhalilll/nuxt-auto-middleware
  ui-components/
    ATelInput/                      # @alikhalilll/a-tel-input
    AGhostSkeleton/                 # @alikhalilll/a-ghost-skeleton
    AInput/ APopover/ ADrawer/      # internal — bundled into the UI packages' dist
    AResponsivePopover/ AUiBase/
apps/
  docs/                             # Nuxt Content docs site (GitHub Pages)
playgrounds/
  nuxt/                             # integration playground — `pnpm play`
scripts/
  release/ build/ pack/ validate/   # the tk CLI — release, build, validate, helpers
```

Each Nuxt-module package exposes three subpaths: `.` (Nuxt module), `./core` (framework-agnostic), `./types`. UI component packages expose `.` (Vue component), `./nuxt` (module auto-register), `./styles.css`, `./resolver`, and feature-specific entries (`./zod`, `./vee-validate`).
